title: Synthesis, Assembly, and Characterization of Monolayer Protected Gold Nanoparticle Films for Protein Monolayer Electrochemistry
protocol: Dissolve 1.1 g tetraoctylammonium bromide (TOABr) in 30 mL of toluene.
Dissolve 0.38 g sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in approximately 20 mL of ultrapure water and chill over ice for at least 30 min.
Dissolve 0.31 g hydrogen tetrachloroaurate (HAuCl4) in approximately 20 mL of ultrapure water.
Quantitatively transfer the HAuCl4 solution to the TOABr-toluene solution using an additional 5 mL of ultrapure water.
Stir rigorously while lightly capped for 30 min.
Transfer both the clear aqueous and burnt orange nonaqueous phases to a separatory funnel.
Discard the aqueous (bottom) layer.
Decant the nonaqueous (top) layer into a clean flask.
Add C6 in a ratio of 2:1 with HAuCl4 to the nonaqueous solution.
Stir for 30 min to form a Au(I) polymer, as detected by a color change from reddish orange to pale yellow.
Transfer the reaction mixture to an insulated ice bath.
Chill to 0°C for at least 30 min with stirring.
Quantitatively and quickly add the chilled NaBH4 solution to the reaction mixture.
Reduce Au(I) to metallic gold in the presence of thiols, forming a thick black solution of MPCs upon addition.
Stir reaction overnight at 0°C.
Transfer the reaction mixture to a separatory funnel.
Discard the aqueous (bottom) layer into a waste beaker.
Rotary evaporate the nonaqueous (top) toluene layer to near complete dryness, leaving a heavy black sludge in the flask.
Precipitate the MPCs by adding acetonitrile and allowing to sit overnight.
Collect MPCs by vacuum filtration using a glass frit of medium porosity with rubber fittings and side-armed flask with aspirator.
Rinse the collected MPCs with a copious amount of acetonitrile.
Allow MPCs to air dry.
Weigh the product.
Characterize MPCs by transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
Analyze MPCs by NMR.
Store capped MPCs for future use.
Drop-cast MPCs dissolved in toluene onto formvar/carbon support film on copper grid (400 mesh).
Operate TEM instrument at 80-100 kV.
Estimate average core size using image analysis software such as Image J.
Electrochemically clean the gold substrate.
Modify the gold substrate with a C6 SAM.
Immerse the gold substrate in alternating solutions of dithiol linking molecules and C6 modified MPCs to form a "dip cycle."
Repeat the dip cycle several times to ultimately form a dithiol-linked MPC film assembly.

Assemble the electrochemical sandwich cell in the following order: first Lucite retainer plate, gold substrate as a working electrode, brass electrical contact to gold working electrode, first rubber gasket, Viton o-ring that defines the electrode area (0.32 cm²), glass cell body, second rubber gasket, and second Lucite retainer plate.
Hold the cell together with threaded rods and carefully tighten wing nuts.
Fit the cell with a commercially purchased reference electrode housing 1 M saturated KCl, Ag/AgCl reference wire, and Pt auxiliary electrode wire.
Perform cyclic voltammetry (CV) in the potential windows from 0.2 to 0.9 V, 0.2 to 1.2 V, and 0.2 to 1.35 V versus Ag/AgCl, KCl at 100 mV/s in a solution of 0.1 M H₂SO₄ and 0.01 M KCl.
Measure the charging current of the cleaned bare gold substrate by performing CV with a potential window from 0.1 to 0.4 V versus Ag/AgCl, KCl scanned at 100 mV/s in KPB.
Discard KPB and rinse successively with UP H₂O, ethanol (EtOH), UP H₂O, and EtOH.
Expose the cleaned gold substrate to approximately 300 μl of 5 mM C6 solution in EtOH and allow it to sit overnight to form an ordered C6 SAM.
Discard C6 solution from the cell and rinse successively with EtOH, UP H₂O, EtOH, and UP H₂O.
Measure the charging current of the SAM at standard conditions.
Discard KPB and rinse successively with UP H2O, EtOH, UP H2O, and EtOH.
Expose the SAM modified gold substrate to approximately 300 μl of 5 mM 1,9-nonanedithiol (NDT) solution in EtOH for 1 hour.
Discard NDT solution and rinse successively with EtOH, UP H2O, EtOH, UP H2O, and methylene chloride (CH2Cl2).
Expose the gold substrate to a methyl pentatriacontane thiol (MPC) solution of CH2Cl2 (~1 mg/mL) with agitation by slowly bubbling with N2 gas for 1 hour.
Discard MPC solution and rinse successively with CH2Cl2, UP H2O, and KPB.
Measure the charging current of the MPC layer at standard conditions.
Discard KPB and rinse successively with UP H2O and CH2Cl2.
Expose the gold substrate to approximately 300 μl of 5 mM NDT solution in CH2Cl2 for 20 minutes with agitation by slowly bubbling with N2 gas.
Discard NDT and rinse thoroughly with CH2Cl2.
Repeat steps 2.7 and 2.8 to deposit the second MPC layer of the film assembly.
With each additional MPC layer, repeat steps 2.9 and 2.10 and observe an increase in charging current.
Rinse the film-modified substrate with KPB.
Inject approximately 150 μL of AZ solution (concentration: 5-10 μM) in KPB into the echem sandwich cell.
Allow the echem cell to sit capped and refrigerated for at least 1 hour.
Remove the echem cell from the refrigerator and allow it to return to near room temperature.
Thoroughly rinse with KPB.
Refill the echem cell with KPB.
Bubble KPB with N2 gas for 10 minutes.
Perform protein monolayer electrochemical studies as CV in the potential window from -0.25 V to 0.25 V (versus Ag/AgCl, KCl) scanned at 100 mV/sec in KPB.
Rinse a 3-MPTMS modified glass slide with CH2Cl2.
Place the slide in a MPC solution of CH2Cl2 (˜1 mg/mL) for 1 hr while agitating on a shaker at low speed.
Rinse the slide thoroughly with CH2Cl2, and dry with N2 gas.
Take a UV-Vis spectrum (from 400 to 1000 nm) of the slide.
Rinse the slide again with CH2Cl2.
Place the slide in a 5 mM NDT solution of CH2Cl2 for 1 hr while agitating on a shaker at low speed.
Rinse the slide with CH2Cl2.
Place the slide in a MPC solution for 1 hr while agitating on a shaker at low speed.
Rinse the slide thoroughly with CH2Cl2, dry with N2 gas.
Take a UV-Vis spectrum (from 400 to 1000 nm) of the slide.
Reattach MPC film assembled on a 3-MPTMS modified glass slide onto a clean, standard microscope slide using Embed 812 epoxy resin.
Mix Embed 812 epoxy resin and allow it to thicken for at least 12 hours.
Fill a "00" BEEM capsule with the thickened epoxy resin and place it on top of the MPC film sample.
Apply pressure to create a seal between the epoxy resin and the MPC film sample, allowing a bubble to rise to the top.
Allow the mixture to polymerize for at least 18 hours at 60°C.
Cool the mounted slides to room temperature.
Heat the mounted slides for 20 seconds on a cast aluminum hot plate at 200°C.
Remove the block with attached MPC en face film using a jeweler's saw.
Reembed the removed portion in a silicon flat mold with the MPC film side up facing the interior of the silicon well.
Fill the silicon well with epoxy resin at room temperature and allow it to polymerize for at least 18 hours at 60°C.
Cool the sample to room temperature.
Obtain thin sample sections of 60-80 nm on a Leica UCT ultramicrotome by cutting sections perpendicular to the knife's edge using a diamond knife.
Place sliced sections on formvar/carbon support film on copper grid.
Take TEM images of prepared cross sections of MPC film assemblies.
Monitor double layer charging current for MPC film growth over 5 dipping cycles.
Collect cyclic voltammograms using a potential window from 0.1 to 0.4 V in potassium phosphate buffer.
Scan cyclic voltammograms at 100 mV/s in potassium phosphate buffer.
Recollect cyclic voltammograms using a potential window from -0.25 to +0.25 V for AZ adsorbed to MPC film assembly.
Scan recollected cyclic voltammograms at 100 mV/s in potassium phosphate buffer.
